bound_context.question: What bytes does the 296-byte leaf routine at 0x630c430 write for a destination, a source and a length, and which path does its own guard select?
bound_context.version_note: node115 embeds ZLIB_VERSION "1.3.1"; these bodies are identical in the zlib 1.3.2 bundled by libz-sys 1.1.31, so the zlib release is not pinned by these windows.

caller_census.contract: memory effect only: the routine is void, so the post-call rax column is the caller's own register reuse, not a returned value
caller_census.method: Capstone disassembly of the artifact; each call site validated at the instruction boundary and attributed to the .eh_frame FDE that encloses it

claim_anchors: semantics.tsv (19 anchors: claim -> target instruction address, bytes and decoded instruction)
environment_limits: Static only: the artifact was never executed, and no source build is claimed.

The model executes the routine's decoded bytes on a small machine model that implements exactly the instructions present (including movdqu/movups) and raises on any other; it models the buffer explicitly rather than relying on host memcpy semantics, which are undefined for overlapping regions.
For overlapping inputs the C-level result is undefined by the C standard; the packet reports what THIS compiled body computes, which is the point of reconstructing it.
capstone 5.0.7 / readelf / objdump were used; results are reproducible with those tools on the digest-verified binary.
ledger: cases.tsv (300 reviewable cases, 75 per family over empty/small/overlap/vector) with a path column and a vector_only_differs column that records where the chunk path would have produced different bytes; the full 2,400-case sweep and a random differential are re-derived in memory by the tests

observations.text: The routine has no return value: the only ret is at 0x630c471, which is also the len==0 target, and rax is used as a loop index (xor %eax,%eax at 0x630c457) rather than a result. caller_use.tsv therefore records each caller's own post-call use of rax (42 sites write it before reading, 2 never read it again) and is NOT a returned-value contract.
lea -0x1(%rdx),%edx with cmp $0x6 and jbe 0x630c455 (0x630c43d..0x630c443) select the byte loop for len <= 7, so the 16-byte path is never entered for a short copy.

observations.claim: the overlap guard keeps the byte loop
observations.text: lea 0x1(%rsi),%rsi / mov %rdi,%rcx / sub %rsi,%rcx / cmp $0xe,%rcx / ja 0x630c478 (0x630c445..0x630c453) take the chunk path only when dest-(source+1) > 14, i.e. the byte loop is kept for 1 <= dest-source <= 15. The subtraction is unsigned, so dest <= source wraps and always takes the chunk path.

The chunk path snapshots 16 bytes (movdqu at 0x630c490) and then stores them (movups at 0x630c496), so a store cannot feed the next load within one chunk; on overlapping regions that produces different bytes than the forward byte loop (movzbl/mov at 0x630c460/0x630c465, which store one byte then read the next). The committed ledger records 96 rows whose chunk-path result differs from the byte-path result.

After the guard, cmp $0xe,%edx with jbe 0x630c548 (0x630c478/0x630c47b) skips the chunk loop for len <= 15; otherwise ecx = (len>>4)<<4 bounds a movdqu/movups loop that advances 16 bytes at a time, and the remainder is copied byte-at-a-time by the unrolled tail block beginning at 0x630c4ca.
Both loops advance their index upward (add $0x1,%rax at 0x630c468, add $0x10,%rdx at 0x630c49a), so neither path copies backwards; the guard is about reads seeing stale stores, not about direction.
The body has no calls and no relocations, and the whole body is one .eh_frame FDE 0x630c430..0x630c558 (296 bytes, 90 instructions).
44 direct calls, 0 tail jumps, in the caller FDEs listed in records.json; each call is validated at the instruction boundary with Capstone and attributed to the FDE that encloses it.
Reading the three arguments as dest, source and a byte count follows from the mangled symbol name and from the loops' byte/16-byte strides; the packet does not prove the C-level types beyond that.

The vendor census note records that node #115 embeds ZLIB_VERSION 1.3.1 while these bodies are identical in the zlib 1.3.2 bundled by libz-sys 1.1.31, so this window does not pin the zlib release; the packet therefore cites the member and the body digest rather than a zlib version.
